label: echoed f as the 1st/2nd copy-phase input (recall_idx 1-2)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase when the fed-back input is the letter f at recall_idx 1 or 2, i.e. the model has just echoed f as original token 0 or 1. Magnitude is strongly modulated by position: when f was the first original token (prev_tok = <DEL>, recall_idx 1) it fires near max (~3.2-3.8; 85% of mass, precision 1.0 for that clause); when f was the second original token (recall_idx 2) it fires weakly (~0.15-0.3 of max) and is often silent for short sequences (L=3-4), which accounts for most false positives. Never fires in the original or delimiter phase, on f at recall_idx >= 3, or on other tokens (a handful of near-zero hits on digit 2 etc.). Insensitive to the token being output and to L beyond the short-sequence dropout.

issues: The claims hold up. On the test split the predicate scores P 0.950, R 1.000, F1 0.974 and mass recall 1.000. On the dev split, all activity is in the copy phase, every active step has recall_idx 1 or 2 (mass shares 0.845 and 0.155), and the input is f on 31,743 of 31,759 active steps.
The recall_idx==1 clause alone has precision 1.000 on test, which matches the claim.

The false positives are systematic, but the explanation already discloses them. They all come from the recall_idx==2 clause in short sequences: with L<=4 its precision is 0.42 (2,820 predicted steps), and with L==4 it is 0.50. With L>=5 the recall_idx==2 clause has precision 0.998.

There are 14 missed steps on test, carrying 0.0% of the mass. They have tiny activations (0.01-0.03) on digits 2 and 3 and on v, at recall_idx 1 in L=3-4 sequences. This is scattered noise, as the explanation says.
The label does not claim more than the predicate. Its wording 'echoed f as 1st/2nd copy-phase input' is accurate, though it doesn't say that the recall_idx 2 response is weak and length-gated.
